normative_extracts.quote: When require-trusted-types-for 'script' is active, DOM injection sinks such as Element.innerHTML and script.src reject raw strings and require a TrustedHTML, TrustedScript, or TrustedScriptURL instance.

browser_support.notes: Supported in Chromium since 2020; polyfill available via trusted-types npm package.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: The DOM parser and script loader reject plain strings at ~60 dangerous sinks unless wrapped by an audited TrustedTypePolicy.

production_failures.symptom: TypeError: Failed to set the 'innerHTML' property on 'Element': This document requires 'TrustedHTML' assignment
production_failures.root_cause: Enabling Content-Security-Policy: require-trusted-types-for 'script' broke a third-party widget writing raw strings to innerHTML.
production_failures.mitigation: Deploy in Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only mode first, then wrap legacy sinks via a sanitized 'default' policy or DOMPurify.sanitize(..., { RETURN_TRUSTED_TYPE: true }).

production_failures.symptom: Wildcard trusted-types * policy allows any bundle to mint unverified TrustedHTML
production_failures.root_cause: Leaving trusted-types * in CSP lets compromised dependencies register pass-through policies that return raw strings.
production_failures.mitigation: Allowlist only named audited policies in CSP: trusted-types dompurify app-sanitizer;
